replicate_statements: Distribution of SMF-derived promoter state frequencies as a function of Pol II ChIP-seq level in Drosophila promoters (n = 5912 promoters).
Promoters were first binned based on their log2 Pol II ChIP-seq signal. Within each bin, the median frequency of each of the promoter state was calculated.
outputs.explanation: The panel reports n = 5912 promoters and specifies that the plotted values are median state frequencies calculated per Pol II ChIP-seq bin across these promoters, giving both the number and type of replicated units.

replicate_statements: The vertical sidebars on the right of the plot depict the frequency of each promoter state determined by single-molecule decomposition.
The percentages of molecules harbouring footprints for the engaged Pol II and PIC are indicated on the right side of the plot.
outputs.explanation: State frequencies for this single locus are derived from 2952 single DNA molecules, and this number and the replicate type (molecules) are stated directly on the panel.

replicate_statements: Distribution of SMF-derived state frequencies as a function of Pol II ChIP-seq level in mouse promoters (n = 6122 promoters).
outputs.explanation: The panel reports n = 6122 promoters, with median state frequencies calculated across these promoters per ChIP-seq bin, matching the reporting standard of panel A.
State frequencies for this single mouse locus are derived from 2871 single DNA molecules, with the number and type of replicate stated on the panel.

replicate_statements: Comparison of PIC state frequency between mouse (TATA-less n = 572 promoters; TATA-containing n = 64 promoters) and Drosophila (TATA-less n = 422 promoters; TATA-containing n = 71 promoters) promoters.
The statistical comparisons between groups were performed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
outputs.explanation: The boxplot compares groups of promoters with explicit n-numbers for each of the four groups (572, 64, 422, 71 promoters) and the replicate type (promoters) is clearly stated, satisfying reporting requirements for the statistical comparison shown.
